principles: Codex Factory is primarily for large, complex, long-term projects, not small daily tasks
v0.4 is a lightweight Process Integrity Layer — it is NOT the final Factory direction
Multi-agent collaboration must be judged in large-project context, not small/medium benchmarks alone
Sunk cost must not determine keep/cut decisions
Emotional reassurance must not determine keep/cut decisions
Evidence and hard logic drive direction, not habit or attachment to existing artifacts
ifMultiAgentDisproven: It should be deprecated with evidence and replaced by an alternative that DOES work for large projects

modeSeparation.researchBenchmark: Controlled experiments comparing Vanilla, Factory Lite, and Agent Company modes
modeSeparation.dailyLightweight: v0.4 core (Manual Router, Proof-of-Read, Evidence Hierarchy, Contamination Logging) for everyday use
modeSeparation.releasePackage: Versioned, SHA256-verified release packages with manifest and forbidden claims
modeSeparation.largeProjectFactory: Full multi-agent orchestration with contracts, scopes, verifier gates, audit trails for complex projects

ifMultiAgentProvenForLargeProjects: It should become the default capability for Codex Factory in large-project context, not an optional edge feature
keyDistinctions: Small benchmark cannot alone decide large-project agent strategy
EVAL-3/RUN-C failure does not prove multi-agent useless — only that 10-role model was overkill for TeamFlow
DRY24 multi-agent success in Factory self-building is SELF_BUILDING_ONLY evidence — not benchmark evidence
